title: Conormal graded algebra on a closed subscheme
statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion] with quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] and powers $\mathcal I^n$ [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. There is a canonical quasi-coherent sheaf of commutative graded $\mathcal O_Z$-algebras $\mathcal G=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal G_n$, called the conormal algebra, characterized by
$$i_*\mathcal G_n\cong\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1},\qquad \mathcal G_0=\mathcal O_Z,\qquad \mathcal G_1=\mathcal C:=i^*\mathcal I.$$
The quotients are sheaf cokernels; $i^*$ is tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], and quasi-coherence is [pqf-def-coherent]. The product of classes of local sections $a\in\mathcal I^m$ and $b\in\mathcal I^n$ is the class of $ab$ in degree $m+n$. The unit is the identity in degree zero. For every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$, put $J=\mathcal I(U)$ and $W=i^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$. There are canonical identifications, compatible with restrictions,
$$\mathcal G_n|_W\cong\widetilde{J^n/J^{n+1}},\qquad \mathcal G(W)\cong\operatorname{gr}_J(R):=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}J^n/J^{n+1}$$
as graded algebras, with the multiplication of [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. For every $z\in Z$, writing $R_z=\mathcal O_{X,i(z)}$ and $J_z=\mathcal I_{i(z)}\subset R_z$, one has
$$\mathcal O_{Z,z}=R_z/J_z,\qquad \mathcal G_z\cong\operatorname{gr}_{J_z}(R_z),\qquad \mathcal C_z\cong J_z/J_z^2.$$
There is a canonical graded algebra morphism
$$\psi:\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_Z}(\mathcal C)\longrightarrow\mathcal G$$
from the symmetric algebra sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-sheaf-construction], whose value on a degree-one generator $c$ is $c\in\mathcal G_1$. Under the canonical identification $(\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal C))_z\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{R_z/J_z}(J_z/J_z^2)$, its stalk map sends $a\bmod J_z^2$ to the degree-one class of $a$. If $X$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], then each $\mathcal G_n$ is coherent on $Z$ [pqf-def-coherent]. The graded algebra sheaf convention is [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures], its quasi-coherence is that of the underlying module [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra], and stalks are the ordinary Zariski module stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk].

proof.text: For each $n\geq0$, construct $B_n$ on $X$ as the sheaf cokernel of $\mathcal I^{n+1}\hookrightarrow\mathcal I^n$, with quotient map $q_n$. The powers are quasi-coherent, so the quasi-coherent cokernel-and-image theorem makes $B_n$ quasi-coherent and gives, for every affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, a surjection $q_n(U):J^n\twoheadrightarrow B_n(U)$ with kernel $J^{n+1}$. Thus $B_n(U)=J^n/J^{n+1}$, and the affine tilde counit identifies $B_n|_U$ with $\widetilde{J^n/J^{n+1}}$. These identifications carry quotient sections to their classes and hence commute with restriction. In particular they concern sheaf cokernels, without assuming sectionwise cokernels on arbitrary opens.

source.place: Tags 0630–0631, definition-conormal-sheaf and equation-conormal-in-degree-n; affine quotient calculation from Schemes Tags 01IB and 01IC

proof.text: Define multiplication directly on local quotient representatives. Given an open $V\subseteq X$ and sections $s\in B_m(V)$, $t\in B_n(V)$, cover $V$ by affine opens $T$ on which step 1 supplies lifts $a\in\mathcal I^m(T)$ and $b\in\mathcal I^n(T)$. Set the local product equal to $q_{m+n}(ab)$. If another pair of lifts is used, refine the intersection of the two affine charts by affine opens $H$. Step 1 identifies the kernel of each quotient map on $H$, so the two restricted lifts differ by $u\in\mathcal I^{m+1}(H)$ and $v\in\mathcal I^{n+1}(H)$. Their products differ by $ub+av+uv\in\mathcal I^{m+n+1}(H)$, and hence give the same quotient section. The sheaf axiom glues these sections to a unique product on $V$, independently of the lifts and cover. Restricting $V$ restricts this local recipe, so multiplication commutes with restriction. Bilinearity and the associative, commutative and distributive laws can be checked on a common affine refinement where all sections lift; there they are the associated-graded ring laws of the cited theorem. The quotient $\mathcal O_X\to B_0=\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I$ supplies the unit, whose two unit identities follow from $1a=a$. Thus the family $(B_n)$ has the graded sheaf algebra structure with exactly the specified product formula.

proof.text: The ideal $\mathcal I$ annihilates every $B_n$: locally lift a section of $B_n$ to $b\in\mathcal I^n$ and multiply by $a\in\mathcal I$; then $ab\in\mathcal I^{n+1}$, whose quotient class is zero. Local vanishing implies vanishing of the section. This also holds for $n=0$.

source.place: Tag 0630, introductory paragraph: the pieces are annihilated by the defining ideal

proof.text: Define $\mathcal G_n=i^*B_n$ using tensor pullback. The closed-immersion annihilation theorem applied to steps 1 and 3 gives quasi-coherence and the canonical unit isomorphism $B_n\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*\mathcal G_n$. The fully faithful closed pushforward, with counit $i^*i_*H\cong H$, shows that this property determines each piece up to its canonical isomorphism. On $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $W=i^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$, the affine pullback theorem identifies $\mathcal G_n(W)$ with $(J^n/J^{n+1})\otimes_R(R/J)$. If $M=J^n/J^{n+1}$, the mutually inverse maps $m\otimes\bar r\mapsto rm$ and $m\mapsto m\otimes1$ are well defined because $JM=0$; replacing $r$ by an element congruent modulo $J$ has no effect, and tensor balancing proves both composites are identities. The affine tilde counit consequently gives $\mathcal G_n|_W\cong\widetilde M$ as an $\mathcal O_W$-module. All maps are induced by quotients, scalar multiplication and pullback units, so commute with restriction.

source.place: Tags 0630–0633, descent to Z and affine description; Morphisms Tag 01QY (lemma-i-star-equivalence), Schemes Tags 01IB and 01I9

proof.text: Pull the operations of step 2 to the pieces $\mathcal G_n$: on local tensor representatives the product is $(\lambda\otimes b)(\mu\otimes c)=\lambda\mu\otimes(bc)$. The $i^{-1}\mathcal O_X$-balancing relations are respected by the bilinearity of $bc$, so this defines the operations on the tensor presheaves and then on their sheafifications. Restriction compatibility and the algebra laws follow on pure tensors; sums of pure tensors locally generate the tensor sheaves. For degree zero the isomorphism of step 4 identifies $\mathcal G_0$ with $\mathcal O_Z$ and the pulled-back unit with its identity. Form $\mathcal G=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal G_n$ in sheaves of modules, with operations extended as in the definition of a graded sheaf algebra. It is quasi-coherent by the coproduct theorem. On an affine $W$ of step 4, the affine tilde functor preserves the coproduct and its unit on global sections is invertible; hence $\mathcal G(W)=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}J^n/J^{n+1}$. Its homogeneous products and unit are exactly those of $\operatorname{gr}_J(R)$. This proves the affine algebra identification as well as the claimed restriction compatibility. The construction uses no assertion that sections on an arbitrary non-affine open commute with infinite direct sums.

source.place: Tags 0630 and 0633, graded algebra and its affine sections; Schemes Tags 01ID and 01LA (coproducts), Modules Section 01CF

proof.text: The quotient $\mathcal I\to B_1$ induces $i^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal G_1$. The affine conormal theorem says that $\mathcal C=i^*\mathcal I$ is quasi-coherent. On $W$ the affine pullback formula identifies this arrow with $J\otimes_R(R/J)\to J/J^2$, $a\otimes\bar r\mapsto ra\bmod J^2$. Its inverse sends $a\bmod J^2$ to $a\otimes1$: a sum of products $\sum j_kb_k\in J^2$ maps to $\sum b_k\otimes\bar j_k=0$, and balancing gives $ra\otimes1=a\otimes\bar r$. Thus the maps are inverse. The affine tilde adjunction identifies their sheaf maps; these local inverses agree on overlaps because they invert the same global arrow. They glue, giving the canonical identification $\mathcal G_1=\mathcal C$.

source.place: Tags 0631 and 0633, degree one and the identity I/I² = I tensor R/I; Morphisms Tag 01R3 (lemma-affine-conormal)

proof.text: Fix $z\in W$ and let $\mathfrak p\supseteq J$ be its prime in $R$, $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak p/J$ its prime in $R/J$. The affine structure-stalk and tilde-stalk theorems give $R_z=R_{\mathfrak p}$, $J_z=J_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\mathcal O_{Z,z}=(R/J)_{\mathfrak q}$. The latter is canonically $R_{\mathfrak p}/J_{\mathfrak p}$: the inverse maps send $\bar a/\bar s$ to the class of $a/s$ and back; the fraction equality criterion makes them well defined. For any $n$, localization exactness applied to $0\to J^{n+1}\to J^n\to J^n/J^{n+1}\to0$ gives $(J^n/J^{n+1})_{\mathfrak p}=(J^n)_{\mathfrak p}/(J^{n+1})_{\mathfrak p}$. Moreover $(J^n)_{\mathfrak p}=(J_{\mathfrak p})^n$: for $n=0$ both equal $R_{\mathfrak p}$; for $n>0$ a product of fractions has numerator in $J^n$, while a generator $a_1\cdots a_n/s$ is $(a_1/s)(a_2/1)\cdots(a_n/1)$; take finite sums. Applying the tilde-stalk theorem to step 4, and identifying localization over $R/J$ with that over $R$ by the same fractions, gives $\mathcal G_{n,z}=J_z^n/J_z^{n+1}$. Stalks commute with the sheaf coproduct, so $\mathcal G_z=\bigoplus_n J_z^n/J_z^{n+1}$. The multiplication sends $([a]/s,[b]/t)$ to $[ab]/(st)$, hence this is an isomorphism of graded algebras with $\operatorname{gr}_{J_z}(R_z)$, not just of modules. Degree one and step 6 give $\mathcal C_z=J_z/J_z^2$. Open restriction does not affect these germs, since neighbourhoods contained in $W$ are cofinal among the neighbourhoods of $z$.

source.place: Tag 0633 (lemma-affine-conormal-sheaf), expanded stalk calculation; Schemes Tag 01HV, Algebra Tag 00CS, Sheaves Section 009E

proof.text: Use step 6 to regard the degree-one inclusion as a linear map $\mathcal C\to\mathcal G$. The quasi-coherent symmetric algebra theorem gives a unique algebra morphism $\psi:\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal C)\to\mathcal G$ extending it. This is the explicitly constructed symmetric sheaf of the statement: the core universal property for that construction and the preceding universal property give maps in both directions, whose composites are identities because they fix every degree-one generator. On every affine $W$ the symmetric algebra affine comparison identifies the morphism with the algebra map $\operatorname{Sym}_{R/J}(J/J^2)\to\operatorname{gr}_J(R)$ induced by $[a]\mapsto[a]$ in degree one. A degree-$n$ product of generators therefore maps to the product of their degree-one classes, which lies in degree $n$; finite sums give the same assertion for all degree-$n$ elements. The commutator relations defining the symmetric algebra are homogeneous, so this proves the map is graded. The affine formulas are restrictions of the unique sheaf map and thus agree on overlaps.

Write $A=R/J$ and $M=J/J^2$ on the affine $W$. The symmetric sheaf is quasi-coherent and has affine sections $\operatorname{Sym}_A(M)$, so its stalk is $(\operatorname{Sym}_A(M))_{\mathfrak q}$ by the affine tilde and stalk theorems. Apply symmetric-algebra base change to $A\to A_{\mathfrak q}$. The identification $A_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_A N\cong N_{\mathfrak q}$ for an $A$-module $N$ is given by $(r/s)\otimes n\mapsto rn/s$, with inverse $n/s\mapsto(1/s)\otimes n$; the tensor relations and fraction equality criterion verify both composites directly. Consequently $(\operatorname{Sym}_A(M))_{\mathfrak q}\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{A_{\mathfrak q}}(M_{\mathfrak q})$, carrying $\iota_M(m)/s$ to $\iota_{M_{\mathfrak q}}(m/s)$. By step 7 its target is $\operatorname{Sym}_{R_z/J_z}(J_z/J_z^2)$. The stalk of the affine map in step 8 sends $\iota_M([a])/s$ to the degree-one class $[a]/s$. Every element of $J_z/J_z^2$ is represented by such a fraction, so this gives exactly the required stalk formula for $\psi$, with its canonical source identification.

source.place: Tag 0632, generator formula under stalks; Algebra Tag 0C6F (lemma-tensor-algebra-localization), Schemes Tag 01HV

proof.text: Assume now that $X$ is locally Noetherian. Choose an affine open cover with Noetherian rings $R$. The opens $W=\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$ cover $Z$; each $R/J$ is Noetherian because an ascending chain of its ideals pulls back to an ascending chain of ideals of $R$, so $Z$ is locally Noetherian. The Noetherian submodule theorem, applied to $J^n\subseteq R$, makes $J^n$ a finite $R$-module for every $n$, including $n=0$. The images of finitely many generators generate $J^n/J^{n+1}$ over $R/J$: coefficients reduce modulo $J$ because $J$ annihilates this module. By the affine finite-type criterion and step 4 each $\mathcal G_n$ is of finite type on this cover, hence on $Z$. It is already quasi-coherent. The coherence theorem for locally Noetherian schemes therefore makes every $\mathcal G_n$ coherent. No Noetherian hypothesis was used in steps 1–9, and no claim of coherence is made for the infinite direct sum.

Proved affine, degree-one and stalk identifications with explicit tensor/fraction formulas, the graded symmetric map with its stalk normalization, and coherence of individual pieces under precisely the stated Noetherian hypothesis. Reused existing DAG tools; no new nodes. Mathematical statement unchanged; added references defining graded sheaf algebra, quasi-coherent algebra and ordinary module stalks.
